Sports.title: Arteta v Alonso, part one: a desire for control and the theory behind the chaos | Jonathan Wilson
Sports.content:
Control v chaos. On the one hand, the forces of order, regimented, playing in precise patterns and, on the other, something darker, more visceral, a method that acknowledges the imperfection of the human soul, the unknowability of football in all its randomness; better, that second way says, to attempt to ride the fury than to believe it might be harnessed.

When it began, a decade ago, that’s how the Pep Guardiola v Jürgen Klopp rivalry appeared. Apollo v Dionysius. Two fundamentally opposed ways of seeing the world. But in time, the two crept towards each other. Klopp moved away from the heavy metal of his Borussia Dortmund years to something more conservative. Guardiola experimented in multiple directions, slowly abandoning the possession-oriented idealism of his past to something less radical but also less predictable.

The temptation, after the first two weeks of the season, is to cast Mikel Arteta and Xabi Alonso in a similar light. Arsenal are yet to concede a goal. They dominated the Community Shield from the first minute, beat a shambolic Manchester City 3-0 and gave the sense that they could easily have won more comprehensively had they been minded to do so. They were no more troubled in beating Coventry by the same scoreline in their opening league game and, while they were rather less dominant, they were still extremely comfortable against Aston Villa on Monday and had been slowly increasing the pressure when Bukayo Saka gave them the lead just before the hour.

Arteta has become more controlling over his seven years at Arsenal, not just in his micromanagement but in his demands from his team. Tactical plans are sophisticated and negotiable only in the final details. In their third successive season of finishing second he spoke repeatedly of the need to reduce, to zero if possible, the xG of the opposition. If they have no chances, they cannot score, and if they do not score, they cannot win.

Last season it was a refrain heard less often; Arsenal did reduce their opponents’ opportunities, conceding seven goals fewer than they had the previous season. There were those who criticised them on aesthetic grounds, bemoaning their reliance on set plays and occasional bouts of excessive pragmatism, but it worked. They were the best team and they won the league, in the end, fairly comfortably. All else is taste, subjective.

Might, it will be asked, there be a more expansive approach this season? Might, with the burdens of yearning and doubt lifted, the insistence on control lessen? Might this be a breezier, a freer and easier, Arsenal? Might that even make them more effective in Europe, more capable of beating Paris Saint-Germain?

View image in fullscreen Bukayo Saka scores Arsenal’s winner at Aston Villa on Monday. Photograph: David Klein/Reuters

Probably not. Arsenal played as they did in the Champions League final out of necessity, not choice. They were exhausted. Only three PSG players had played more than 2,000 minutes in the league last season; nine Arsenal players had – and given the relative strengths of the Premier League and Ligue 1, theirs were harder minutes. In such circumstances an open game is impossible.

Accepting the role played by fatigue, in fact, has been one of Arsenal’s great strengths; last summer’s business was characterised by the accumulation of squad depth over acquisition of the very highest quality. This summer has been about upgrading where possible. They’ve seemingly done that well in midfield and at the back, although losing three players who can operate from the left wing while signing only Christos Tzolis seems a risk, even with Max Dowman likely to be more involved. It’s possible, likely even, that a more relaxed outlook will allow Arsenal to play with a greater freedom but it would be a surprise if the tactical emphasis were not still on control.

Chelsea’s case is more complex; the sense of chaos of Alonso’s opening two games has surely not been deliberate. He is no Kloppite; his heritage is of John Toshack and Rafa Benítez, Vicente Del Bosque and Guardiola. Like Arteta, four months his junior, he came through the youth ranks at Antiguoko in San Sebastián; they are not so different in their formation. When Alonso won the league at Bayer Leverkusen, they had 62% possession. Although they pressed hard, they were not part of the high-tempo, high-turnover Bundesliga trend. Yet in beating Fulham 3-2, Chelsea had 38% possession, and in beating Brighton 4-3 they had only 26%.

Game state is partly responsible. In both games, Chelsea had the lead early and could afford to allow their opponents the ball. The front three of João Pedro, Cole Palmer and Morgan Rogers have excelled playing on the break. There have been glimmers of the sort of interactions Leverkusen produced, the modifications that prevent Alonso’s 3-4-2-1 from experiencing the blockishness that means the formation is more often a tool for counterattacking sides, most notably when Maxence Lacroix advanced from central defence to set up Rogers’ goal against Fulham. But they take time to develop; perhaps the idea for now, as patterns are assimilated, is to lean into the basic simplicity of shape, the security the two screening midfielders in front of the back three should offer.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

View image in fullscreen Chelsea have won their opening two Premier League games this season. Photograph: Allstar Picture Library Ltd/Nigel French/Apl/Sportsphoto

The problem is, it hasn’t yet worked – although that may in part be down to personnel. Having sold Enzo Fernández without signing another central midfielder, though, Chelsea look short in midfield (in as much their bloated squad can look short of anything). If Roméo Lavia can remain fit, and if Reece James’s minutes can continue to be rationed, the issue should not be insoluble, but Moisés Caicedo’s knee problem complicates things, especially with Alonso seemingly unwilling yet to trust the 22-year-old Argentinian Valentín Barco from the start. Without Caicedo, that is not a midfield that is going to create much, and may struggle even with ball retention.

It’s possible that on Sunday, in a game Chelsea are not expected to win, it is easier to maintain shape and discipline, that a destructive pairing works more naturally. Only by making the game a midfield slog to be decided by which team’s forward line can best exploit breakdowns can Chelsea feel they have an edge. That may end up looking like control against chaos, like possession against turnovers. It may even be so. But for Alonso that is a matter less of ideology than of expediency.

Sports.title: Armstrong spurns golden chance to win derby as Birmingham and Wolves draw
Sports.content:
If only Adam Armstrong, the Wolves striker presented with a golden chance three minutes from time, had finished with the same style as his teammate Jackson Tchatchoua when scoring one of the season’s most memorable own goalsbefore half-time, then César Peixoto’s team would surely be sitting in second place in the Championship.

Instead, Armstrong lifted his shot over an open goal and Birmingham deserved to extend their unbeaten start to the league season as they capitalised on Tchatchoua’s howler.

Tom Wagner was back in the St Andrew’s directors’ box for the first time since a stroke in early February and the Birmingham chairman was treated to a thrilling derby. Spoils were shared but fans of the home side, extending their unbeaten start to the season, ended the happier after they twice came from behind to deny their recently relegated neighbours a place back in the automatic promotion frame.

Fer López scored in the third minute for Wolves and, after Jay Stansfield equalised in controversial circumstances, Ladislav Krejci gave the visitors the lead again just after the half hour. But then came a moment that could haunt Tchatchoua for some time. The Cameroon right-back was under no pressure as he went to turn a long diagonal from Phil Neumann back towards his goalkeeper – but instead looped the ball wide and over José Sé and into his own goal.

It was the moment that set the tempo for the rest of a game and reminded Wolves that, despite retaining the majority of their Premier League squad after last Tuesday’s transfer deadline, sheer quality of player alone will not mean promotion.

View image in fullscreen Adam Armstrong (left) reacts to his missed chance to win it for Wolves at Birmingham. Photograph: Nick Potts/PA

López was involved in the build-up before Raúl Jiménez’s pass out to Rodrigo Gomes invited the cross to the near post from which the Spaniard sidefooted home his third goal of the season.

Gomes should have put Wolves 2-0 up in the 19th minute. Christoph Klarer’s poor touch invited Jiménez to steal the ball and put in the winger who, after scoring twice in last Saturday’s 4-1 win over Stoke, looked confident as he angled on goal. But his dink invited James Beadle to produce a fine save.

Stansfield appeared to handle Patrick Roberts’ fine ball into his path but there was no doubting the emphatic manner in which the striker lashed the ball into the near top corner.

Krejci, the Czechia captain, is one of the elite players Wolves were delighted to keep hold of this summer. He may be disappointed not still to be playing in the top division but his bullet header, after André flicked on Hugo Bueno’s corner, gave Wolves a quick endorphin boost.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

It was short-lived however as Tchatchoua lobbed home his tragi-comic own goal. Jiménez struck the crossbar, as he did in Tuesday’s 4-2 defeat at West Ham, but then again, Neumann headed against the same woodwork midway through the second half.

Both sides had a big shout for a penalty – Jiménez went down under Bright Osayi-Samuel’s challenge in the first half, August Priske under André’s in the second – but as Birmingham, their tails up along with their fans’, dominated possession after the break Wolves had the clearest of many chances for both teams to win the game, in the 87th minute.

López dispossessed Demarai Gray from a long ball into the area and, faced with the goalkeeper, unselfishly squared for Armstrong. One of the Championship’s most proven goalscorers somehow contrived to lift the ball over the empty goal from 10 yards out.

There was still time for Birmingham to think they had won it as Marvin Ducksch arced his free-kick towards the top corner. There, however, was Sá, another surprising retainee at Wolves, to show why he was awarded a new contract this season to tip the ball aside and ensure this pulsating derby finished even.

Sports.title: Glasner claims VAR was ‘guessing’ after Forest are denied winner against Spurs
Sports.content:
Oliver Glasner argued there was insufficient evidence to disallow Neco Williams’s goal against Tottenham, accusing the video assistant referee Peter Bankes of guessing that the Nottingham Forest defender handled and said ruling it out weakens the officials’ authority. Midway through the second half, Williams stooped to head in on the goalline as Sandro Tonali attempted to hook the ball clear after Morgan Gibbs-White’s deflected effort bobbled towards the net.

Glasner conceded at least one angle showed Williams appeared to handle the ball, seemingly to protect himself as Tonali went to clear the ball with his left boot, but said the footage was too unclear to disallow the goal. “I don’t think VAR can intervene when he’s guessing,” said Forest’s head coach. “It was not clear and obvious. We had a briefing before the season that the threshold for VAR intervention should be very high and this is why it was a wrong intervention for me.

“I’ve watched five or six different angles and to be fair, from one angle you can guess that the ball touched the arm because the shirt [of Williams] moves a little bit, but it’s not clear whether it’s [because of] the ball or Tonali on the goalline. I know refereeing a Premier League game is really difficult – refereeing a training session is sometimes really difficult – but we are told to support the referee, to keep the threshold for VAR intervention very high, to strengthen the referee’s decision and they didn’t do that today. With these kinds of situations, you weaken the referees.”

Bankes checked the goal and then the referee, Craig Pawson, took to the mic before awarding a Spurs free-kick amid a chorus of boos from the home support: “After review, the ball touches the hand of Nottingham Forest’s No 3 before the goal is scored.” Williams was adamant he did not handle the ball. “I headed it in between my arms,” said the Wales defender, who this week signed a new four-year contract. “If you’re going to pause it, it’s going to look like it hit my arm but it didn’t. I have seen all the images and at not one moment can you tell that has clearly hit my arms because it never. I knew straight away I’d headed it down in between my arms.”

The disallowed goal was undeniably the moment of an underwhelming contest. For the third successive league match, Tottenham failed to score and this time they did not even muster a shot on target. Dominic Solanke heading on to the roof of the Forest goal, 88 minutes on the clock, was as threatening as they got. Omar Marmoush wellied a shot wide after Spurs countered at speed. Mykhailo Mudryk was brought off the bench for his first competitive minutes for 645 days after a doping suspension but Spurs were blunt. Aside from a 5-1 win against a Charlton B team in the Carabao Cup, their season so far reads: five goals against and none scored.

View image in fullscreen Spurs’ Mykhailo Mudryk came on as a late substitute for his first competitive appearance for 645 days. Photograph: Andrew Boyers/Action Images/Reuters

Apart from Gibbs-White’s effort in the buildup to the disallowed goal, Forest’s only other shot on goal was a daisy-cutter from James McAtee. The Spurs league debutant Sávio, a £75m arrival from Manchester City, showed a few neat touches but he and Destiny Udogie were withdrawn after an hour on the advice of Tottenham’s medical department. “I’m not happy when we have the plan but it is for my advantage, my business, the management of the players after their injuries,” said De Zerbi, who accepted his team lacked quality in the final third. “We have to make better decisions, to keep more calm when we are very close to do something important.”

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

No wonder both teams remain winless. Spurs’s date at home to Everton next weekend has taken on another layer of significance and the same applies to Forest’s trip to Aston Villa. Vinai Venkatesham, the Tottenham chief executive in attendance, could be forgiven for wondering when Spurs will see the fruits of their £300m-plus spend, much of the focus on sharpening their attack. They turned to Mudryk, who thrived under De Zerbi at Shakhtar Donetsk, after the failure to sell Richarlison halted moves for preferred targets Cody Gakpo and Iliman Ndiaye. This was not the desired result. “We bought very, very good players but you can’t just build the team with the names like in Football Manager,” De Zerbi said.

Sports.title: High-flying Hull stay unbeaten by holding off Aston Villa in stalemate
Sports.content:
It’s never dull in Hull, as the saying goes in these parts, and after just three games the Premier League is proving to be quite some ride for Hull City supporters.

Having embarrassed Manchester United here on the opening day and won at Coventry last weekend, this deserved point and third successive clean sheet merely reinforced Sergej Jakirovic’s belief that his men can beat the drop.

You have to go back to Bolton’s excellent start in 2001-02 to find a promoted side who began the season with three straight victories. The Tigers failed to emulate Sam Allardyce’s team, but they came closest to a winner as the Algeria winger Mohamed Belloumi hit the crossbar with a stunning second-half shot before the substitute Mohamed-Ali Cho and Oli McBurnie threatened late on.

“We could have won, but they also had a few chances in the second half,” said Jakirovic, who signed a two-year contract extension on Friday. “We won’t be ungrateful for seven points after three games and another clean sheet. It’s a great result for us and we showed we can compete at this level.”

For Aston Villa, it was another largely impotent display which saw them fail to score for the third match running as the captain, John McGinn, and Emiliano Buendía spurned decent second-half opportunities.

Villa failed to manage a shot on target when being hammered 4-0 at Brighton and losing 1-0 at home to Arsenal; here they managed just one, a tame shot by George Hemmings early on.

Unai Emery chose to take the positives from Villa’s display as he patiently rebuilds the club after a summer of major upheaval which saw a number of key players leave and 10 new faces arrive.

View image in fullscreen George Hemmings had Aston Villa’s first shot on target of the Premier League season, 13 minutes into their third game. Photograph: Craig Brough/Action Images/Reuters

“The result is not enough, but I think we deserved more,” he said. “We weren’t clinical but of course to win matches, you need goals. We created chances today to score and we must improve but we are rebuilding.”

Ambition pulsed loudly at a sold-out MKM Stadium before kick-off as a huge amber banner inscribed with the words “One family, one dream” was paraded on the pitch. It said much for the togetherness that Jakirovic has fashioned within his squad and the connection with the club’s supporters during a remarkable few months in the Tigers’ history.

Desire was visible and audible in the stands and on the pitch, but Villa almost led inside the second minute when Nicolas Jackson headed Ian Maatsen’s teasing left-wing cross wastefully wide.

Hull were unfazed and Belloumi beat Ross Barkley twice, including with a delightful nutmeg, before breaking clear down the right flank. His low cross was cleared, but it hinted at the possibilities on offer for the hosts.

In the 13th minute, Villa finally fashioned their only effort on target this season as Hemmings’s low shot was comfortably saved by Konstantinos Tzolakis.

If Villa could not see off a promoted side widely tipped for an immediate relegation this season, could they really consider themselves ready to start climbing the table? A neat passing sequence should have brought a Villa goal in the 50th minute but McGinn could only lift the ball harmlessly over Tzolakis’s crossbar from less than 12 yards out.

Three minutes later, Villa went even closer as Hemmings outstripped the Hull captain, Lewie Coyle, down the left flank and showed intelligence to pick out Buendía with a neat cut-back. Buendía should have buried the chance but he blazed wildly over, much to his disgust.

In the 65th minute, Hull went agonisingly close to scoring when Belloumi collected possession from a short corner and curled a stunning left-foot shot against the bar. There was a resilience to the hosts, and the collective desire that carried them to promotion last season will be needed over the next 35 games if they are to defy the odds and beat the drop.

It was evident again late on when the Hull substitute Lucas Herrington – on his 19th birthday – produced a vital block to repel Tyrone Mings’s shot. Cho’s close-range effort was then repelled by Zion Suzuki before McBurnie failed to properly connect with Giles’s cross as Hull looked likeliest to nick a late winner.

Sports.title: Haaland edges Manchester City past Coventry as Fernández sparkles on debut
Sports.content:
Enzo Fernández started for Manchester City after Nico O’Reilly’s back injury during the warm-up and sparkled, showing why the club paid a British-record-equalling £125m for the midfielder. The winner came courtesy of Erling Haaland’s 300th goal in club football and Fernández had a key part, feeding Antoine Semenyo, whose cross from the right was crashed home.

In the second half Coventry hammered away, but their wait for a first top-flight goal since Mustapha Hadji’s second in a 3-2 defeat at Aston Villa on 5 May 2001 goes on. The visitors did not like losing, but were heartened by holding the star-studded hosts to a slender win, though the bottom line is all three of their Premier League outings on their return have been defeats.

Frank Lampard said: “I don’t think we deserved to lose. I’m disappointed we didn’t get what we deserved – which was a point. We can walk out of here with our heads held extremely high.”

Enzo Maresca’s men have a maximum nine points so can be supremely satisfied. “Today was not a nice win, a bit ugly,” he said. “In the first half we deserved more goals – we scored one but could have scored one or two more.”

The manager said of Fernández: “The reason Enzo was on the bench [initially] was because he arrived only a few days ago. I know how frustrating it was for him in the last weeks but in the end he played some minutes and was quite good. Nico felt something in his back – not serious.”

Ayyoub Bouaddi, bought for £85m, was on the bench for the hosts, as Fernández lined up alongside Rayan Cherki in a 4-1-2–2-1 that had Semenyo and Iliman Ndiaye, another new home signing, stationed behind Haaland.

View image in fullscreen Enzo Fernández shoots on his Manchester City debut. Photograph: Phil Noble/Reuters

Coventry, with Ethan Pinnock and Frank Onyeka replacing Caleb Yirenkyi and Loum Tchaouna from the XI that lost at home to Hull, could have taken the lead when Abdukodir Khusanov played the ball back to Gianluigi Donnarumma and it slipped under the goalkeeper’s boot, but the Italian scrambled it clear. The visitors should then have bridged the 25 years to Hadji when a Semenyo pass meant for Rúben Dias was intercepted by Taiwo Awoniyi. But when the striker ran in his radar failed, and the shot was pulled wide.

The longer Coventry stayed level the better their prospects. Cherki fed a galloping Haaland and he twisted and let fly, but Carl Rushworth’s save was equal to the shot. Then, dazzling Cherki footwork – after a pass from Fernández – was followed by an effort that struck a post.

The frame of the goal and Rushworth could do nothing to stop Haaland’s opener. This time Fernández curved a pass in behind for Semenyo, the right-winger spun the ball over, and Haaland did the rest.

This was 26 minutes in and Coventry were under siege. Fernández collected the ball along the right, looked up and aimed a cross for Haaland but it failed to beat the first man. Then Cherki, again in Fred Astaire mode, made space and saw an effort blocked.

Maresca wants his wingers to be more direct – utilising the pace of Ndiaye and Semenyo – and the tactic spun Coventry. So, too, did an impish Cherki flick which put Haaland in again: he rode a challenge when going down might have brought a penalty, before shooting. Rushworth once more thwarted the Norwegian.

View image in fullscreen Frank Lampard and the Coventry players applaud their fans but their wait for a Premier League goal goes on. Photograph: Phil Noble/Reuters

For Coventry, Jack Rudoni did better than Awoniyi with a header at close range, but Donnarumma flew to his left to prevent an equaliser. This showed the hope Lampard’s men carried but they had to finish any chance as these were scarce.

Ndiaye was fairly quiet on debut and when Cherki’s work took the ball to him in the area he should have pulled the trigger but refused.

Maresca said of the Senegalese: “Ili just had two sessions with us – most of the time he was moving in the wrong way, he needs to learn. When Marc Guéhi has the ball [at centre-back] he was dropping a lot – we didn’t need that, we needed him in the final third, that space was for Josko [Gvardiol, the left-back].”

The manager was more enthused about Elliot Anderson. “Really impressed not just today, he was very good against Palace, and against Bournemouth,” said Maresca. “The best thing with Elliot is day by day he wants to be better.”

Bouaddi’s home debut came on 75 minutes for Fernández and the 18-year-old showed composure during Coventry’s late-game bombardment, which included Ellis Sims forcing a point-blank save from Donnarumma.

Sports.title: Scottish Premiership: Celtic’s Yang completes fightback to see off St Mirren
Sports.content:
Yang Hyun-jun scored the winner as Celtic came from behind to beat an impressive St Mirren side 2-1. St Mirren were heading for the top of the Premiership when Nikolas Agrafiotis netted from the spot midway through the first half.

Liam Scales conceded the penalty with a handball but made amends when he headed home six minutes after the break. And Yang finished off a counterattack midway through the second half after good pressing from Camilo Durán.

The victory in Paisley made it five wins from five league games for the champions and inflicted St Mirren’s first Premiership defeat. Martin O’Neill’s side were made to work all the way by a Saints side who played with tempo, invention and managed 19 shots at goal.

O’Neill later lamented the unavailability of Yang for some crucial games – the 24-year-old will now fly to Japan for the Asian Games and miss the midweek trip to St Johnstone and two games against Rangers, plus the Europa League opener against Ferencvaros.

“We are going to miss him. He’s in really fine form at the moment,” the manager said. “But he’s signed off with a brilliant goal. He’s in great form and he’ll work for you going backwards. He doesn’t mind doing the hard graft.”

Rangers striker Ryan Naderi accepted a gift to score the only goal against Motherwell at Ibrox, but they fear their captain Lawrence Shankland faces a lengthy spell on the sidelines after a hamstring injury suffered early on in the game.

Naderi, who came on for Shankland in the eighth minute, dispossessed Alex Paulsen as the Motherwell goalkeeper attempted to dribble the ball past him outside his box and the German had the simple task of rolling the ball into the net to score what proved to be a 12th-minute winner.

Motherwell dominated possession and created several chances but Rangers were more effective in the final third and should have added to their lead. Kim Min-su missed a first-half penalty and the debutant striker Kevin Kelsy was among those to pass up good opportunities after he came off the bench.

View image in fullscreen Lawrence Shankland leaves the pitch unaided but his manager later revealed the club fear his hamstring injury is significant. Photograph: Steve Welsh/PA

Rangers ultimately saw out the game without any late scares as they recorded a third consecutive Premiership victory.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Of Shankland, the Rangers manager, Derek McInnes, said he fears the injury is similarly significant to the one that kept him out for two months early in 2026. McInnes said: “He has a similar feeling to the hamstring injury he had at Hearts last January. We don’t want to speculate too much but he says it feels similar, in the same area, so we’ll get him scanned on Monday.

“He says he felt fine going into the game and there was nothing really that he did in the game that he was aware of, he just felt it pull up. It’s a shame for the boy because he was obviously in good form, getting himself moving and enjoying some of that attacking threat we’ve had over the last few games, and we’ve waited long and hard for that.”

Michael Forbes scored an added-time equaliser for Dundee United against Falkirk, who had led at Tannadice thanks to Jacob Murrell’s fourth-minute opener, while Kilmarnock picked up their first point but are still waiting for a first Premiership win of the season after a 0-0 draw at Aberdeen. Kilmarnock’s Aaron Tshibola was sent off for a second yellow card after 83 minutes but the hosts could not find a way past the 10 men.

Sports.title: Ferrari's Charles Leclerc suffers 160mph crash - suspending F1's Italian Grand Prix - just after team-mate Lewis Hamilton raged at him forcing him off the track
Sports.content:
Ferrari's Charles Leclerc suffers 160mph crash - suspending F1's Italian Grand Prix - just after team-mate Lewis Hamilton raged at him forcing him off the track

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Charles Leclerc was left sitting in pain on the grass after suffering a dramatic 160mph crash at the start of the Italian Grand Prix.

The Ferrari favourite lost control of his car at the final bend, the Parabolica, on the second lap as he duelled with Oscar Piastri for fourth place.

Leclerc’s impact with the wall was severe with only a short portion of gravel to slow his trajectory into the hoardings, which he thudded side-on.

The Monegasque soon jumped out of the car but then sat disconsolately on the grass as he was comforted by a marshal before being taken away in the medical car. He was feeling his neck as he went for treatment. Ferrari said he had been released from the medical centre without injury.

The race was red-flagged and some fans in the grandstands cried at the huge blow for their team.

Charles Leclerc spins off at the Parabolica turn and crashes into the barriers

Leclerc was seen with his head in his hands on the grass after the heavy smash

The two Ferraris came together with Hamilton (left) dropping several places as a result

By this point, Leclerc had already squeezed Lewis Hamilton on the second part of the opening Del Refillo chicane and was driving somewhat erratically. Hamilton was furious, saying: ‘Charles pushed me off.’

The seven-time world champion, who started fourth, fell down to 10th place.

George Russell was leading the race for Mercedes when the race was suspended after passing pole man Pierre Gasly on the main straight at the end of the first lap.

Leclerc’s stricken car was taken away by crane.

Organisers announced the race would resume at 2.39pm, UK time.

Sports.title: Leicester City fans turn on 'disgraceful' manager Russell Martin over his 'throwing under the bus' interview after they lost 4-0 at home in League One, 10 years after Premier League title
Sports.content:
Leicester City fans turn on 'disgraceful' manager Russell Martin over his 'throwing under the bus' interview after they lost 4-0 at home in League One, 10 years after Premier League title

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Some Leicester City fans are turning on Russell Martin after his comments following their latest disappointing result.

The Foxes were thumped 4-0 at home by Oxford United in League One on Saturday afternoon.

It was their heaviest-ever defeat in the third tier and sees the club sitting 17th in the table with just one win alongside two draws and two defeats.

Leicester were tipped by many to come straight back up to the Championship after suffering a second-straight relegation from the Premier League to League One. It's even more galling for the club who were crowned Premier League champions 10 years ago.

However, that has not proved to be the case - with Russell citing their young team as a reason why Saturday's result happened. Russell, who lasted just 123 days at Rangers before he was sacked last season, included five players in his starting XI under the age of 23, including two teenagers. The five substitutes they brought on were aged 18, 19, 20, 21 and 23.

'I'm not concerned about that happening again,' he told BBC Radio Leicester.

🦊#LCFC | Russell Martin says today’s 4-0 defeat against Oxford United was ‘unacceptable’.



Leicester City have won 1️⃣ game out of their opening 5️⃣ in League One.



🔗 https://t.co/NHbU8Q5AYD pic.twitter.com/z9qex2FNGY — BBC Sport Leicester (@BBCRLSport) September 5, 2026

Leicester City manager Russell Martin is under-pressure from fans after his post-match interview following their 4-0 defeat by Oxford United

'I feel I understand what's happened today with so many young guys and a tough moment. We can't quite get through it and after a big, busy period.

'We will be better for it. We have a week now and we have to make sure we put it right next week.'

He then added: 'We had a lot of players who were doing a third game in a week for the first time in their careers, but it's not an excuse.

'But I think that's the learning now - we have to find a team on the pitch, especially in a three-game week that can deliver a consistent level of aggression and a consistent level of energy because the last three games we have built so much energy, so much feel-good factor about it.

'The players and staff, the fans have been brilliant and we had to build on the win on Tuesday night and today we have done the opposite.'

That viewpoint didn't go down with supporters on social media with one writing: 'He just can't help himself. Blaming the kids at the end… wow. The one thing the fans have really got behind is the young players, and you've just thrown them under the bus.

'Not sure how you come back from this, Russell Martin.'

That was echoed by other angry fans. One user put: 'Leaders lead from the front, take responsibility and face it head on …not this poor excuse as a manager, blaming younger players and not his tactics and choice of captain, disgraceful.'

Another wrote on X: 'This is worse than we thought... He doesn't think this is on him, his tactics & his suicidal style of play.. but inexperience & three games a week instead!

'Takes some balls to be having your pants pulled down by the likes of St Mirren/Falkirk/Burton/Oxford & still be this delusional.'

Another angry Leicester fan commented: 'Nonsense. We were exposed today by every single issue that was there in the other two games this past week.

'The only naivety (stupidity) is from the manager.'

Since guiding Southampton to the Premier League via the 2023-24 Championship play-offs, Martin has won only three of his last 28 league matches across two years with three different clubs (Southampton, Rangers and Leicester) - for an 11 per cent win ratio. His time at Scottish giants Rangers saw him win just one of his seven league matches, drawing five and losing the other. Across 17 games in all competitions there he recorded just five victories.

Martin will be hoping to turn around Leicester's form and his critics' anger when they travel to Stockport County on Saturday afternoon.

Sports.title: Police launch investigation into Cardiff City's ex-Arsenal star 'grabbing young fan by the throat' - as Portsmouth call incident a 'safeguarding matter'
Sports.content:
Cardiff City's Krystian Bielik is at the heart of a police investigation after he appeared to grab the throat of a young Portsmouth fan during their 2-0 Championship defeat on the south coast. The bizarre incident occurred in the 70th minute at Fratton Park, with Cardiff trailing 2-0 to the hosts on Saturday. As former Arsenal academy graduate Bielik attempted to gather the ball from the stands, a Portsmouth supporter beat him to it and threw it away from him. That act caused the 28-year-old to be aggrieved with Bielik seen reaching out towards the fan's throat and pushing them away. The fan responded by standing up and appearing to try to push Bielik in retaliation. Following a delay, the supporter involved in the incident was ejected from the stadium for their part in the incident while Bielik avoided punishment. And on Sunday afternoon, Hampshire Police announced that an investigation into an alleged assault is underway, as per BBC Sport. So Bielek grabs a kids throat, kid defends himself, and kid gets thrown out. Portsmouth FC should give off about this and Bielek needs suspending! pic.twitter.com/9Np1k8Xl3i — Charlie Barnes (@ChaltJames) September 5, 2026 Cardiff's Krystian Bielik appeared to grab the throat of a young Portsmouth fan after they threw the ball away from him. Police have now launched an investigation into the incident The fan was ejected from the stadium following the incident, while Bielik avoided punishment 'We can confirm that we are investigating an incident in which a teenage boy was reportedly the victim of a common assault during the football match at Fratton Park. Our enquiries are ongoing,' the police said. Portsmouth also released a statement confirming that it was now being handled by the police and was the subject of a 'safeguarding matter'. 'Portsmouth Football Club are aware of supporter concerns regarding the incident involving a young fan and an opposition player at yesterday's match at Fratton Park,' their statement begins. 'As this remains a safeguarding matter and is currently under investigation by both the club and the police, it would be inappropriate for us to comment further on the circumstances at this time. 'However, we are aware that a number of claims and assertions are circulating on social media. We would urge caution against speculation while enquiries are ongoing. 'The welfare and safeguarding of young people are of paramount importance to Portsmouth Football Club. We will continue to liaise with the relevant parties as enquiries progress. 'No further comment will be made at this stage while investigations remain ongoing.' Both Portsmouth manager John Mousinho and his Cardiff counterpart Brian Barry-Murphy were spoken to by the referee, as well as captains from both teams. Portsmouth would ultimately go on to secure a 2-0 victory over their newly promoted opponents. Bielik, 28, was making just his fourth appearance for Cardiff after joining the Bluebirds last month. Barry-Murphy claimed post-match that Bielik 'got slapped in the face' by the fan and praised the referee's handling of the incident. 'I wanted to make sure he (Bielik) was protected and make sure he was okay, which he is. 'I thought the referee and his staff handled the incident impeccably. 'He said he'd seen everything which occurred really clearly, so he defused the situation and implemented the correct processes from there. 'The players are always subjected to different things that's not acceptable. 'My job is to protect the players, but really I'm trying to make sure that we play well and win. 'I'm sure the FA will look at it and implement the correct processes.' Portsmouth boss Mousinho offered an apology to Cardiff and their players following the incident. 'The referee said that, as Krystian went to get the ball, there was a little bit of a kerfuffle and one of the supporters struck him. 'It wasn't a good incident. I have just seen him there, and he was OK, but that's not the point, we can't be having that. 'We want to create a really difficult atmosphere at Fratton Park, we have done that successfully over the past few years. 'Sometimes it tips over, I understand that, I don't think it needs to tip over to that extent. 'We extend our apologies to the players, Cardiff and make sure we can try to cut it out.'

Sports.title: Arsenal v Chelsea combined XI - according to the stats: It's an all-blue attack but who wins 7-4 on stars included between the champions and the title pretenders?
Sports.content:
Arsenal v Chelsea combined XI - according to the stats: It's an all-blue attack but who wins 7-4 on stars included between the champions and the title pretenders?

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

We're only on the third weekend of the season but already we have a big London derby on our hands – with Xabi Alonso taking his Chelsea side to take on his great friend Mikel Arteta and Arsenal this Sunday.

The Gunners will be looking to continue the perfect start to their title defence, while Chelsea – who have also won two from two – will hope to prove they can contend with last season's champions.

Old friends reunite for this grudge match and statisticians at Sofascore have ranked the best combined XI based on this season's stats. So read on to see the team – and find out who wins the player count 7-4...

Goalkeeper: Emiliano Martinez

Sofascore rating: 8.10/10

Martinez's first game with Chelsea after signing from Aston Villa, less than a week ago, may, on paper, have made fans nervous given he conceded three goals.

But the goalkeeping position has been seen as one of Chelsea's main weaknesses with Robert Sanchez around, and the former World Cup winner goes straight into this combined XI.

Despite David Raya not conceding a goal this season, Martinez edges him when it comes to the ratings – perhaps due to the Arsenal man only facing one shot on target so far this term.

Emiliano Martinez (pictured) gets the nod ahead of David Raya in between the sticks

Right back: Ben White

Sofascore rating: 7.73/10

The 28-year-old remains one of Arsenal's most dependable players, continuing to be a cornerstone in Arsenal's defence.

White has been dribbled past twice during these first two matches and has just under ten clearances, helping his side to two consecutive clean sheets.

The defender's passing has also been a highlight, with White registering an assist in his side's opening league appearance against Coventry.

Centre back: Josh Acheampong

Sofascore rating: 7.10/10

The 20-year-old is one of the younger faces in Chelsea's squad. Despite that, the young defender has made appearances in both Premier League matches, and an appearance in Chelsea's Carabao Cup victory against League One Luton, who are managed by ex-Arsenal midfielder Jack Wilshere.

Acheampong's stellar performance as one of the starting XI against Fulham showed his potential; he won four tackles and six ground duels, and also blocked two shots.

A player linked with leaving Chelsea this summer could now be an important cog in Xabi Alonso's side this season.

Centre back: Maxence Lacroix

Sofascore rating: 6.97/10

Lacroix arrived at Stamford Bridge this summer with a sizeable price tag – £52million – but it already seems Chelsea have landed a defensive stalwart for their club.

The FA Cup and Europa Conference League Winner ranks top amongst his teammates in both clearances (12) and tackles (sic), carrying on his defensive work rate from Crystal Palace by anchoring Chelsea's defence.

Maxence Lacroix has been impressive at the heart of Chelsea's defence so far this season

Left back: Riccardo Calafiori

Sofascore rating: 7.57/10

The Italian left back's 25/26 season was plagued by injuries, and he will be hoping to make more of an impact this campaign – and he's off to a good start.

Thanks to his standout performance against Aston Villa, he won the man of the match award, completing 19 out of 21 passes, winning five duels, one tackle, one interception and, for good measure, assisted the only goal of the match.

The 6ft 2in defender is also averaging 2.5 clearances a game, helping Arsenal keep clean sheets in both games so far this term.

Right winger: Bukayo Saka

Sofascore rating: 7.47/10

Arsenal's longest-serving player remains a bright spark on their right flank.

In the opening two games of the season, he has had 12 touches in the opposition's box, which is the sixth-most in the Premier League.

The Hale End graduate has scored two goals too, including the winner against Aston Villa last time out, and is leading the charge of the current Gunners side.

Bukayo Saka has shone for Arsenal this season, netting twice in his side's first two games

Centre midfield: Cole Palmer

Sofascore rating: 8.17/10

SofaScore highest rated player heading into Sunday's game battled a groin injury for much of last year, so Chelsea fans' nerves were on edge watching him get subbed off against Fulham in their league opener.

But they needn't worry – the 24-year-old has played in both Premier League matches so far and in the Carabao Cup – showing he is as healthy as ever.

Chelsea are the highest scoring team in the league so far, largely in thanks to Palmer. He has had six shots, scoring two of them, and added an assist too.

Centre midfield: Martin Odegaard

Sofascore rating: 7.93/10

Arsenal's captain is a steady presence for the Gunners as they look to repeat last season's success.

The Norwegian has been at the core of Arsenal's resurgence under Mikel Arteta.

Odegaard scored against Coventry in the season opener and is top of Arsenal's tackling ranks, helping to keep them top of the table.

Attacking midfield: Morgan Rogers

Sofascore rating: 7.57/10

Chelsea fans can only be ecstatic by one of the biggest transfers of the summer in Rogers. The newest squad member is carrying on from his time in Aston Villa with high production in the final third.

Rogers' ability to drive through the midfield ranks him as one of the most dangerous ball carriers in the division, averaging the most expected assists (1.11) per game.

Scoring a goal and recording one assist so far in this campaign, the £117million man looks more than worth it for Chelsea.

Cole Palmer (left), Joao Pedro (centre) and Morgan Rogers (right) have been a devastating trio so far this season

Centre forward: Joao Pedro

Sofascore rating: 7.67/10

Pedro shoulders most of Chelsea's goal scoring responsibility. He fought off competition from Liam Delap for the starting striker position last season, with Delap being sold to Nottingham Forest in the summer.

The good news is he looks completely up to task – that point was driven home by scoring in the first minute against Fulham.

The Brazilian's talent has been on full display so far this season, recording a goal and an assist in both matches played. Pedro's tenacity is felt in the scoring for Chelsea, but his opponents feel it in conflict, with the Brazilian winning 17 duels in two games in the Premier League – the fourth most in the league.

Centre forward: Danny Welbeck

Sofascore rating: 7.50/10

Eyebrows were raised when Xabi Alonso brought 35-year-old Welbeck and 36-year-old Jordan Henderson in the summer.

But it signifies a clear stamp of identity in a side that struggled to have one in previous seasons, with the Spaniard looking to add experience to his squad.

Though Premier League game time has been limited, Welbeck did get a run out against Luton in the League Cup, amassing two shots on target and converting one.

He has scored three Premier League goals in 12 appearances against the Gunners. He'll be hoping to add to this, should he get the call up to lead the line at some point in the game.

Sports.title: Man City's former chairman says their £440m transfer spend makes a MOCKERY of the Premier League's regulation amid their 115 charges case - and that 'justice delayed is justice denied'
Sports.content:
Man City's former chairman says their £440m transfer spend makes a MOCKERY of the Premier League's regulation amid their 115 charges case - and that 'justice delayed is justice denied'

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Manchester City's former chairman David Bernstein says his old club's transfer spending while their 115 charges case continues in silence 'makes a mockery' of the Premier League's regulation of the top division.

Bernstein, who was City chairman from 1998 until 2003 and served as Football Association chair 2011-13, today attacked the lack of an outcome and questioned the Premier League's handling of the case.

City, who spent £440million in the transfer window and equalled the British transfer record signing £125m Enzo Fernandez, kicked off this season still without resolution to their infamous financial charges case.

City were charged with 115 alleged breaches of the Premier League's financial rules in February 2023 and a 12-week hearing concluded in December 2024 - but an independent commission is still yet to publish its ruling on the 'hugely complex case'.

The club strenuously deny the allegations. The verdict could see City exonerated or facing historic penalties.

Now Bernstein, 83, has joined the growing chorus of criticism of the delays - after Premier League chief executive Richard Masters admitted a verdict 'has taken longer than expected'.

Erling Haaland celebrates taking Manchester City to the top of the Premier League again

This is the fourth season to begin under the cloud of the City 115 charges announcement.

Writing in the Sunday Times, Bernstein said: 'The fact they have done this (transfer spend) against the background of the 115 Premier League charges is extraordinary and makes a mockery of regulation in England's top division, supposedly the best-run league in the world.

'Why the league decided to prosecute all 115 alleged offences is a mystery to me. Surely common sense (often in short supply) would point to simplifying the process by taking a handful of the bigger, clearer issues and pursuing these as specimen cases.

'Justice delayed is justice denied, and the longer this process is drawn out, the more the resulting implications and challenges are compounded.'

It was a bumper summer for City after the exit of long-serving manager Pep Guardiola. They also signed Elliot Anderson (£116m), Ayyoub Bouaddi (£86m), Iliman Ndiaye (£60m), Allan and Geronimo Rulli.

Masters has claimed that City's ongoing 115 charges saga is 'not necessarily top of the list' when it comes to his conversations with clubs.

David Bernstein was City chairman from 1998 until 2003 and served as FA chair 2011-13

Four Premier League sides have reserved the right to seek compensation should City be found guilty and it would appear that much of football is desperate for an outcome.

However, Masters suggested that the noise in boardrooms up and down the country is not as loud as one might imagine.

'I obviously speak to clubs all the time,' he said last month. 'It's not necessarily a topic of conversation that is top of the list. (There are) Lots of other things to talk about and do. The Premier League moves on. It's starting (again) on Friday evening.'

Masters has previously admitted to being frustrated by the length of time the independent panel is taking to return its verdict.

'The process is the process,' he said. 'It will resolve itself. But as you know, I literally can't say a thing about it. There's only one available option, which is to allow the process to reach its natural conclusion. I can't talk about the substance of the case. I can't talk about the timing of the case. Our rules are very clear about that. I understand that people are frustrated but it will take as long as it takes.'

The Premier League's latest domestic broadcast deal has seen the amount paid per game fall by around £2.5m.

Some have wondered if that is an indicator that fans are getting fed up of various litigations, with Nottingham Forest, Everton and Leicester City docked points in recent times.

But when asked if the perceived lenient penalty, a £10m fine handed to Chelsea for repeated backhanders, suggested there was a desire to move on from docking points, Masters denied that was the case.

'I don't think litigation and broadcast deals are necessarily associated,' he said. 'I do think litigation is to be avoided.

'It should be a last resort within a league system or generally. I think that is generally the attitude that is taken by stakeholders in the game. Litigation is a last resort.'

City are top of the Premier League, having taken maximum points from their first three matches under the guidance of Enzo Maresca - including a 1-0 victory over promoted Coventry City on Saturday.

Sports.title: 'I found out I wasn't in Man Utd squad on social media after deadline day move was blocked'
Sports.content:
'I found out I wasn't in Man Utd squad on social media after deadline day move was blocked'

Manchester United left one former star in the dark when he reportedly discovered his squad snub via social media

View 2 Images Ex-Man United stopper Sergio Romero was denied an exit from the club after learning he'd failed to make the squad on social media (Image: Getty )

Former Manchester United goalkeeper Sergio Romero was devastated to discover he'd been left out of the squad via social media in 2020. The former Argentina stopper moved to Old Trafford from Sampdoria in 2015 but endured six uneventful years with the English giants.

‌



Having been a regular at club and country level during the earlier stages of his career, Romero was originally brought in as backup for David de Gea. However, he was rarely used by United in higher-priority competitions and made just 61 appearances for the club.

‌



His United tenure hit a new low ahead of the 2020/21 season when he was left out of their Premier League squad. This came after ESPN reported he was priced out of a move away, with Everton refusing to pay the £10million exit fee United allegedly insisted upon.

‌



Having made 17 appearances in all competitions for United the previous campaign, Romero found himself entirely sidelined in the 2020/21 campaign. The South American failed to record a single outing for the club and was finally allowed to leave on a free in 2021 when he joined Venezia.

FOLLOW OUR MAN UTD FB PAGE! Latest United news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Romero, 39, won the Europa League, FA Cup and EFL Cup during his stint at Old Trafford. However, his squad snub left a bitter taste in the mouth of those closest to the goalkeeper.

‌



Man Utd stars' feelings on two transfers emerge as Luke Shaw verdict given READ MORE :

Unai Emery makes telling Alejandro Garnacho comment as ex-Man Utd star slumps to new low READ MORE :

The matter was made worse by speculation Romero had learnt of that development through social media. And the rejection led to his partner going public herself to dig the club out over their tactics.

"He helped the team reach four finals/semi-finals and then was left on the bench only to lose them all," wrote Romero's wife, Eliana, on Instagram at the time. "It is time for them to return the opportunity and let him go. RESPECT FOR ONCE!!!

View 2 Images Romero kept 39 clean sheets in 61 games for United (Image: PA)

‌



The Toffees were one of several suitors reportedly interested in a move for Romero on deadline day in 2021. However, the Liverpool outfit weren't prepared to pay the supposed £10m price tag attached to the then-34-year-old.

Romero's place in the United pecking order suffered at the time after Dean Henderson returned to the club. That left him and veteran Lee Grant as Ole Gunnar Solskjaer's preferred backups behind De Gea in both the Premier League and Champions League.

In another Instagram post, Eliana wrote: "It is a very sad day because he desired the chance to go to another club. He has worked hard every day for this, because he gives his all for United and I think that his chances of playing for United have gone down.

"This doesn't sound right to me. It doesn't appear honest or professional or serious that they have to let him go. I am very sad because of this."

Sports.title: Gary Neville jumps to defence of Liverpool icon in 'disrespect' argument with Jamie Carragher
Sports.content:
Gary Neville jumps to defence of Liverpool icon in 'disrespect' argument with Jamie Carragher

Gary Neville and Jamie Carragher clashed during a live segment on Sky Sports while talking about Arsenal striker Kai Havertz and former Liverpool star Roberto Firmino

View 3 Images Gary Neville and Jamie Carragher clashed in a heated segment (Image: Sky Sports )

Gary Neville accused Jamie Carragher of disrespecting former Liverpool striker Roberto Firmino while making a comparison with Arsenal's Kai Havertz.

‌



Havertz has emerged as Mikel Arteta's first-choice forward for the 2026/27 campaign, with the German starting ahead of Viktor Gyokeres so far. The versatile forward, who joined the Gunners from Chelsea for £65million in 2023, scored in the Community Shield win over Manchester City and the 3-0 victory over Coventry on the opening weekend.

‌



The 27-year-old is not a prolific goalscorer, having only once reached double figures in a Premier League season, but his all-round game is highly valued by Arteta. He is sure to have a key role in Arsenal's title defence after they failed to sign a forward in the closing stages of the transfer window.

‌



The Gunners failed to convince Julian Alvarez to return to the Premier League from Atletico Madrid after Real Madrid star Vinicius Junior also turned them down.

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

‌



Neville feels that, while Havertz is a proven performer for Arsenal, he lacks the star power that they may need. And his opinion, plus a comparison with Liverpool great Firmino, caused a stir in a debate with Carragher on Sky Sports Super Sunday.

Neville: "I think having Havertz up front means the centre-backs can afford to edge over to his side a little bit more, because Havertz is a good player, he's a very good performer, but he's not going to frighten the life out of you."

Carragher: "It didn't stop Mo Salah with Firmino."

‌



Neville: "No, no, no. Please, don't disrespect Firmino in terms of what a player he was by the way."

View 3 Images Kai Havertz is a key player for Arsenal (Image: Stuart MacFarlane/Arsenal FC via Getty Images)

Carragher: "In terms of goalscoring."

‌



Neville: "He was unbelievable in the way in which he was a foil for Mane and Salah, it was essential."

Carragher: "So why can't Havertz be that kind of player?"

Neville: "I don't think Havertz is as good as Firmino in any way shape or form."

‌



Firmino returned 111 goals and 76 assists in 362 games over eight years for Liverpool and formed a sensational front line with Sadio Mane and Mohamed Salah. Under Jurgen Klopp's management, the Brazilian won the Premier League, FA Cup, Champions League and Carabao Cup.

View 3 Images Roberto Firmino was a key part of Liverpool's famous front line (Image: PHIL NOBLE, POOL/AFP via Getty Images)

While he played as a No.9, Firmino was known to drop deep, link up play and create space Salah and Mane on the flanks. It is a similar game plan to Arteta at Arsenal, where Havertz leads the line ahead of Christos Tzolis, Bukayo Saka and Martin Odegaard.

‌



Havertz has 38 goals and 18 assists in 114 appearances for Arsenal so far. While Arsenal won their first Premier League title in 22 years last season, he managed seven goals and five assists in all competitions, with just two of those strikes coming in the league.

But having returned from a knee injury, the Germany international will play a key role for the Gunners as they attempt to defend their title.

Sports.title: Jamie Vardy finally decides next club as Leicester icon signs one-year deal
Sports.content:
Jamie Vardy finally decides next club as Leicester icon signs one-year deal

Jamie Vardy will play for Burnley in the Championship this season after finally putting pen to paper on a deal with the Clarets amid speculation over his future

View 2 Images Jamie Vardy has signed for Burnley (Image: Getty Images)

Jamie Vardy has signed for Burnley on a deal until the end of the season.

‌



The Leicester icon, 39, has been without a club since leaving Italian side Cremonese at the end of last season. He had been linked with a shock move to Everton after they failed to land a striker on deadline day.

‌



But Vardy has now penned a deal with Burnley following their relegation from the Premier League.

‌



The Clarets have endured a chastening start in the Championship, mustering just two draws and three defeats from their opening five games, leaving them bottom of the table.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

“I’m really happy to now be here at Burnley FC," he said. "This club has a proper footballing history and passionate fans who deserve a team that represents them and their town.

‌



"I can’t wait to get going on the pitch and help the team move in the right direction.”

Burnley boss Nicky Hayen added: “We are delighted to welcome Jamie to Burnley FC. His experience and leadership will be invaluable to our squad, and we believe he can make a significant impact on our campaign.

"Jamie has a proven track record, and we are looking forward to seeing him in a Claret shirt.”

‌



View 2 Images Vardy in action for Leicester against Sheffield Wednesday (Image: Ben Roberts Photo/Getty Images)

Vardy was the subject of interest from home and abroad following his departure from Cremonese. As well as Everton, boyhood club Sheffield Wednesday were linked as were West Ham, Wrexham and Sao Paolo in Brazil.

Vardy wrote his name into English football folklore by firing Leicester to the most unlikely title win in history in 2016. He also won the FA Cup and two Championship titles with the Foxes.

Article continues below

He played 26 times for England, scoring seven goals.

Sports.title: Police launch investigation after Cardiff City star appeared to grab young fan by the neck
Sports.content:
Police launch investigation after Cardiff City star appeared to grab young fan by the neck

Cardiff City defender Krystian Bielik clashed with a young Portsmouth supporter during the Bluebirds' 2-0 defeat at Fratton Park on Saturday afternoon

View 2 Images Krystian Bielik clashed with a Portsmouth fan

Hampshire Police have launched an investigation into an alleged common assault after a Cardiff City player appeared to grab a young Portsmouth supporter by the neck during a clash on Saturday.

Portsmouth's 2-0 win over the Bluebirds was overshadowed by unsavoury scenes in the 70th minute of the Championship match. Krystian Bielik went over to the sidelines to collect the ball in order to take a throw-in, only to become involved in a heated exchange with a nearby fan.

Replays appeared to show the 28-year-old former Arsenal star grabbing the youngster by the throat. Bielik was then slapped by the fan, who was led out of the stadium by stewards along with his family. The match was briefly stopped by the referee in order to cool the situation down.

Hampshire Police are now investigating the incident, which will also be the subject of a Football Association investigation after being included in the referee's report.

A Hampshire Police spokesperson told Mirror Football: "We can confirm that we are investigating an incident in which a teenage boy was reportedly the victim of a common assault during yesterday’s (Saturday 5 September) football match at Fratton Park. Our enquiries are ongoing."

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

Article continues below

Portsmouth said in a statement: “Portsmouth Football Club are aware of supporter concerns regarding the incident involving a young fan and an opposition player at yesterday’s match at Fratton Park.

“As this remains a safeguarding matter and is currently under investigation by both the club and the police, it would be inappropriate for us to comment further on the circumstances at this time. However, we are aware that a number of claims and assertions are circulating on social media. We would urge caution against speculation while enquiries are ongoing.

“The welfare and safeguarding of young people are of paramount importance to Portsmouth Football Club. We will continue to liaise with the relevant parties as enquiries progress. No further comment will be made at this stage while investigations remain ongoing.”

A Cardiff City spokesperson said: "Cardiff City FC is aware of a confrontation between a small section of Portsmouth supporters and Krystian Bielik at Fratton Park yesterday.

View 2 Images Krystian Bielik joined Cardiff this summer (Image: Adam Fradgley/Getty Images)

"We are satisfied with the way that match officials dealt with the situation during the game, having been in full view of it. Player protection will always be of paramount importance to us.

"It is understood that due process will be undertaken following the submission of the referee’s report to the Football Association. As such it would not be appropriate to comment further on the matter at this time.”

Speaking after the game, Cardiff boss Brian Barry-Murphy said: "I wanted to make sure he (Bielik) was protected and make sure he was okay, which he is. I thought the referee and his staff handled the incident impeccably. I was assured by him the correct processes will take place.

"He said he’d seen everything which occurred really clearly, so he diffused the situation and implemented the correct processes from there.

Article continues below

"The players are always subjected to different things that’s not acceptable. My job is to protect the players, but really I’m trying to make sure that we play well and win. I’m sure the FA will look at it and implement the correct processes."

Sports.title: Unai Emery makes telling Alejandro Garnacho comment as ex-Man Utd star slumps to new low
Sports.content:
Unai Emery makes telling Alejandro Garnacho comment as ex-Man Utd star slumps to new low

Alejandro Garnacho has endured a very difficult few seasons and his loan spell with Aston Villa appears to have got off to a tricky start following his switch from Chelsea

View 2 Images Garnacho is set to spend the season on loan with Aston Villa (Image: Getty Images)

Aston Villa boss Unai Emery believes Alejandro Garnacho still needs time to adapt having played just half an hour for the club. The Argentine forward joined Villa on loan this summer from Chelsea.

‌



There is an obligation to make that move permanent at the end of this season should certain conditions be met. But Garnacho’s contributions in the Midlands have been limited so far.

‌



He has made just three substitute appearances for Villa so far this season, while he has also fallen behind academy graduate George Hemmings in the pecking order. Asked how he has managed to earn that position, Emery has suggested that the youngster is already a Premier League player, while Garnacho still has work to do.

‌



Speaking after his side’s 0-0 draw with Hull City on Saturday, Emery said: “George, he worked last year the whole year with us and played minutes. He is performing fantastic and getting better.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

“He created one assist for Buendia. He is working in the intensity and kilometres we need. He is doing it. I think he is a player now, clearly, to be in the Premier League.

‌



“Then, we have other players who joined who need to adapt to us in training, playing matches, and Garnacho is in this way.

“We need their performance to try to add things, working and getting numbers. Garnacho is in this way. How he is responding, George, is really fantastic.”

Garnacho’s move to Villa follows a very tricky couple of years for him. He fell out of favour at Manchester United, ahead of a switch to Chelsea.

‌



View 2 Images Garnacho has yet to start for Aston Villa this season (Image: Getty Images)

But he lasted just a year at Stamford Bridge, scoring just once in 24 Premier League appearances. He underlined his desire to rediscover his confidence during his time with Aston Villa.

"This is an important club which is going up really quickly, so I can't wait to get started here," Garnacho said after his switch to Villa was announced. "I was looking for a club to get my confidence back, so I can try to become the player I was a few years ago in my first years at Manchester United.

Article continues below

"I spoke with the manager and he gave me the confidence to try to help the team here - that's why I'm here. It is important to play in European competitions and the Champions League is the best one, so the fact we are playing in it this season makes me really happy. Hopefully we can do something important in it."

Sports.title: Milos Kerkez makes alarming admission about Andoni Iraola's Liverpool tactics
Sports.content:
Milos Kerkez makes alarming admission about Andoni Iraola's Liverpool tactics

Liverpool picked up their first win of the season under Andoni Iraola's management against Ipswich on Friday night, but Milos Kerkez admission may ring alarm bells

View 2 Images Milos Kerkez says Liverpool are still adapting to Andoni Iraola's style (Image: Justin Setterfield/Getty Images)

Milos Kerkez has hinted that Liverpool must find a compromise because they cannot carry out Andoni Iraola's high-pressing tactics for 90 minutes.

Liverpool picked up their first win of the season by beating Ipswich 2-0 on Friday night. Alexander Isak netted both goals inside the opening 10 minutes, with Cody Gakpo providing both assists in an encouraging performance.

The Reds also managed to claim their first clean sheet of the campaign following consecutive 2-2 draws against Newcastle and Nottingham Forest. There was a debut for £123million signing Bradley Barcola, while fellow new arrivals Victor Munoz, Jeremy Jacquet and Ronald Araujo all contributed.

It was an important step for Liverpool, who have undergone a turbulent summer since Arne Slot's departure, with sporting director Richard Hughes following FSG chief Michael Edwards out the door on Saturday.

FOLLOW OUR LIVERPOOL FB PAGE! Latest Reds news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

Iraola is known for his high-intensity pressing tactics when his team are out of possession. Kerkez played under the Spaniard at previous club Bournemouth so knows better than most what Iraola demands - and his admission post-match was intriguing.

"When you press like us, it's a bit tough to do it for all the game and all the 90 minutes," he told the club website. "We can do it for the first 30 to 35 minutes and in some ways we can do that in the second half at the beginning – but then it's all about staying compact and talking to each other.

"That's what we said also that we need to improve, and as defenders we are happy with the clean sheet. We defended pretty well their crosses and the set-pieces. Like I said, everyone was 100 per cent focused."

Asked if Iraola's style was coming across now, he replied: "Yes, definitely. I think everyone felt better on the pitch and I think myself also when I look at it I'm getting more into the play and better.

View 2 Images Andoni Iraola's tactics may take time to work for Liverpool (Image: AP Photo/Dave Shopland)

"Obviously it's a clean sheet, particularly away we know it's tough in the Premier League everywhere. We're happy but we can't celebrate too much – now games come every three days and it's onto the next."

Iraola was happy but level-headed in his assessment of the Ipswich win. "We needed this win and as well with the performance – especially [in the] first half we have been a very good team," he said.

"We put a lot of pressure to the opposition and I think we started really strong in the game. I think that we learned, probably, the lessons from the last two games where we conceded early goals and today we didn't want this to happen, and we were really strong in the first half.

"In the second half also, I think in a different way. We controlled the game, we defended well, but we didn't have this threat offensively, probably. But overall, I think it's a game to finish quite pleased [about]."

Article continues below

Liverpool's squad depth, and their understanding of their manager's demands, will be tested as they begin their Champions League campaign against Atletico Madrid on Wednesday night at Anfield. They then host Fulham on Saturday in the Premier League before a Carabao Cup tie against Tottenham on September 15.

Sports.title: Arsenal missed out on two transfer targets 'due to Andrea Berta's approach'
Sports.content:
Arsenal missed out on two transfer targets 'due to Andrea Berta's approach'

Arsenal spent heavily in the summer transfer window as they attempt to reclaim the Premier League title but a number of deals did not come off for the Gunners despite Andrea Berta’s best efforts

View 2 Images Andrea Berta's attempts to sign Page and Monga ended in frustration (Image: Getty Images)

Arsenal reportedly missed out on a double deal for Leicester wonderkid’s Jeremy Monga and Louis Page due to Andrea Berta’s unconventional negotiation tactic. The Gunners were linked with the pair as part of a recruitment drive that has seen them hoover up a number of the country’s most promising youngsters.

‌



They have already signed Igor Tyjon from Blackburn Rovers, Manchester United’s James Scanlon as well as Cardiff City starlet Axel Donczew. The North London side have also agreed a deal to sign Georgian youngster Andria Bartishvili.

‌



Arsenal were keen to add Monga and Page to that list, the pair having made a huge impression in the East Midlands but summer switches did not come to fruition. According to BBC Sport, Arsenal’s sporting director Andrea Berta chose to conduct negotiations with intermediaries as opposed to with Leicester colleagues, which is not an unusual move for him, having done the same with the move for Bruno Guimaraes.

‌



But a lack of club-to-club contact on this occasion was cited as a reason as to why moves were not completed. Instead, Monga chose to switch to Premier League rivals Manchester City for £12m, while he has subsequently joined Championship side Swansea City on a season-long loan.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

Page in the meantime ended up staying with Leicester despite late interest from Manchester United. Despite that, Arsenal boss Mikel Arteta remains satisfied with a window that has seen the side spend close to £200m.

‌



Asked if he was relieved if the window was closed, the Spanish coach replied: “It is what it is - we don’t decide! I think we all know we had to make a decision on when we wanted the window to be closed, and now that’s it, and now it’s crystal clear everybody’s squads and where everybody has to be."

On if there was any deals that got away, he said: “I don’t know - I think every moment, every situation is different. Sometimes we need to react because something unexpected happens as well, and you need to be prepared for that, so I think every case is different.”

View 2 Images Arsenal were interested in both Louis Page and Jeremy Monga (Image: Getty Images)

‌



Arteta added: “I don't know, these are just opinions. The window is closed and I prefer to look at all the incredible things that we have in this squad and not to spend any more time on the things that are not part of us right now. That's it and that's my main responsibility.

“Yeah, 100% ticked. The outcome after can be different to what you expect, but the intention is certainly there, which is, in my opinion, what I value the most.”
